modules.name: patients
modules.description: Patient registration and lookup. Logs the full registration payload - including SSN and DOB - via print() for debugging. get_patient does SELECT * and returns every column to any caller regardless of role. list_patients has no pagination or per-provider filtering.

modules.name: appointments
modules.description: Appointment scheduling and lookup by patient. No check for double-booking the same provider at the same time.

modules.name: records
modules.description: Clinical notes: add and search. Both routes build SQL via string interpolation/formatting. Search has no access control tied to the requesting provider, and nothing in this module writes an audit trail despite every call touching PHI.

modules.name: shared
modules.description: Not a domain module - infrastructure. Flask app factory and sqlite connection helper. Owns the patients/appointments/medical_notes schema.

entry_points.description: POST /patients - register; logs full payload including SSN/DOB in plaintext.
GET /patients/<id> - SELECT * returns every column to any caller.
GET /patients - list all, no pagination or per-provider filtering.
POST /records - add clinical note, string-formatted INSERT.
GET /records/search - string-formatted LIKE query, no access control, no audit trail.

coupling_notes.description: appointments.patient_id is a real foreign key into patients, so appointment data can't be understood or migrated independently of the patients table.

deep_dive_notes: Churn is uninformative this run - the whole tree was introduced in a single commit, so every module shows churn_commits=1.
PII/PHI is logged in plaintext at registration (patients/routes.py) via a bare print() - this ends up in whatever log aggregation exists with far looser access control than the database itself.

get_patient's SELECT * with no field-level authorization is the single highest-severity finding: any caller who can reach the route at all gets SSN and DOB back, not just providers actively treating that patient.

records/routes.py has the target's only SQL injection surface (both create and search), and it's in the module handling clinical notes specifically - the same code smell family seen in other example targets, but the domain context (PHI, not generic app data) meaningfully raises its severity.
No audit trail is written anywhere in the target, despite patients, appointments, and records all handling PHI - there's no record of who accessed or searched what.
No tests exist anywhere in the target. No input validation on any route.
